metadata.note: TWO FIDO2 keys declared on a machine that has NONE — the case a person hits when they own fewer keys than they declared, or left one in a drawer. The VM cannot hold a real FIDO2 token, so what this proves is everything AROUND the enrolment: the plan names one item per key (cryptroot:fido2, cryptroot:fido2#2), `luks_token_policy.enroll_failure: warn-and-continue` turns the failed enrolment into a red warning instead of a dead install, the install COMPLETES and the machine boots, the skipped keyslots are never recorded as enrolled (so the next plan still asks for both), and `sync` invents nothing. At a terminal a human is asked per key and can answer `s` instead — that path is unit-tested, since there is no terminal here. Autologins root + ships python so it can be driven. NOT for real hardware.
